hook_text: A sheep on a Karoo farm and a jersey in a city shop. How many kinds of work are in between?
clip_script: Graaff-Reinet, a Karoo sheep farm. Shearers clip the wool from merino sheep. That wool is a raw material, a primary product, taken straight from nature. In a factory, it is washed, spun into yarn and knitted into a jersey. Now it is a manufactured good, a secondary product. A truck driver delivers it, and a shop assistant sells it. Those are services. Raw materials, manufactured goods and services: the three things people trade.
visual_style: Whiteboard sheep being shorn, wool flowing into a factory, a jersey appearing, then a truck and a shop counter.
mood: Warm and steady, like following one thread all the way.
pacing: One step of the journey per beat, labelling each kind of product as it appears.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort ten things at home into raw materials, manufactured goods and services.
